text:
Washington is a team that keeps finding new ways to win games it shouldn't be comfortable in. Saturday's 4-3 win over Florida came after Tom Wilson was thrown out for boarding, and the Capitals scored three straight at even strength without him. That's the encouraging version of this team: 54% of the five-on-five expected goals, a 60% playoff chance in our simulations, and a lineup with enough new pieces that the coaching staff is still sorting it out.

The newcomers have been the story. Alex Tuch, whose departure from Buffalo is still producing headlines, scored Saturday and plays on the only line Tom Gulitti of NHL.com noted stayed intact through this week's shuffle, with Dylan Strome and Jordan Kyrou (56% of the chances). The new Aliaksei Protas, Pierre-Luc Dubois and Ryan Leonard line produced the winning goals against Florida. Boone Jenner, Justin Sourdif and Leonard won 73% of the chances in their minutes together before the shuffle.

The worries are the old guard and the penalty box. Wilson has no points in ten games on 5.5 expected goals, and Alex Ovechkin has two points in ten on 4.7. Both should come around, but Wilson may now face a suspension. Washington takes 4.4 penalties a game and draws 3.5, and the penalty kill allows 0.87 expected goals a night. Logan Thompson, pulled earlier in the week, steadied things Saturday. Watch whether the shuffled lines hold.
